question_text: Find the derivative of √(x + 1) from the first principle with respect to x.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what you multiply by, and why the h then cancels.

steps.label: State the first principle
steps.margin_note: First mark. Substituting gives √((x + h) + 1) = √(x + h + 1). Put h inside the root before doing anything else.

recall.must_convey: That the first principle is written with f(x) = √(x + 1) and f(x + h) = √(x + h + 1).
accept: write the first principle with f of x equal to root x plus one
f of x plus h is root of x plus h plus one
take the limit of root x plus h plus one minus root x plus one over h
first principle rasta, root x plus h plus one ani rasta
start from the definition of the derivative

steps.why: The definition is the marked move. The whole of x + 1 sits under the root, so x + h + 1 does too — writing it any other way loses the question.
common_mistakes: Substituting h in place of x + h.
steps.memory_tip: The whole of x + 1 sits under the root, so x + h + 1 does too.

steps.label: Multiply by the conjugate
steps.margin_note: Two marks: one for choosing the conjugate, one for the h cancelling. (√a − √b)(√a + √b) = a − b is what removes the roots from the top.
lines: Putting h = 0 here gives 0/0, so simplify first.

recall.must_convey: That the quotient is multiplied above and below by the conjugate √(x+h+1) + √(x+1), the top becomes h, and the h cancels.
accept: multiply top and bottom by the conjugate of the two roots
root a minus root b times root a plus root b is a minus b
the numerator becomes h and it cancels with the h below
conjugate tho multiply cheste roots poyi h migulutundi
rationalise the numerator so the h cancels

steps.why: Putting h = 0 in the original quotient gives 0/0, so the h below has to be removed first. The conjugate turns the top into a − b, where the two x + 1 terms cancel and only h is left.
common_mistakes: Multiplying by √(x+h+1) − √(x+1), the same expression again, which does not clear the roots.
Cancelling h before the numerator has been simplified to h.
Subtracting only part of the bracket and writing x + h + 1 − x + 1.
steps.memory_tip: A difference of two square roots on top: multiply by the same two roots added. The roots then go.

steps.label: Take the limit
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The two roots are now equal, so they add to 2√(x + 1). The answer holds for x > −1, where the root is defined.

recall.must_convey: That the two equal roots add to 2√(x + 1), giving 1/(2√(x + 1)).
accept: the two roots become equal so they add to two root x plus one
the answer is one by two root x plus one
derivative of root x plus one is one over two root x plus one
one by two root x plus one answer vasthundi
put h equal to zero in the denominator

steps.why: Once h has cancelled, the expression is continuous at h = 0, so the limit is simply its value there.
common_mistakes: Writing 1/√(x + 1) and forgetting that the two roots add.
Writing 2/√(x + 1), with the 2 on the wrong side of the fraction.
steps.memory_tip: Two equal roots add, they do not multiply: √a + √a = 2√a.

insider_note: The form is 0/0, so multiply by the conjugate — no trigonometric identity helps here. The h cancels and substituting h = 0 leaves 1/(2√(x + 1)).
